title: The Last Total Solar Eclipse
topic: Total solar eclipses exist because the Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon and about 400 times farther away; the Moon recedes 3.8 cm a year, so in about 600 million years (if that rate holds) it will be too small to cover the Sun

beats.narration: One day, this will happen for the last time.
It only works by luck. The Sun is about four hundred times wider than the Moon, and about four hundred times farther away. A perfect fit.
But the Moon is leaving, almost four centimeters a year. Every year, the fit gets worse.
In about six hundred million years, if it keeps that pace, the Moon will be too small. A ring of fire is all that's left.
phrases: A ring of fire is all

beats.narration: So we got the good seats. By accident.
phrases: So we got the good seats.
